recognize_zh: CD3 染色下濾泡間（副皮質）區佈滿棕色陽性 T 細胞，而多個濾泡呈淡藍色幾乎不染，清楚勾勒出小型萎縮濾泡的輪廓；T 細胞屬正常分布，無異常聚集。
features: Low-power (4x) CD3 immunostain of lymph node
Dense CD3-positive small T cells filling the interfollicular/paracortical areas
Several small follicles largely CD3 negative, outlining regressed follicular structures
Scattered CD3-positive cells along vessels traversing interfollicular zones
No aberrant T-cell sheets or loss of CD3 in the interfollicular compartment
describe_en: CD3 immunohistochemistry at low power shows abundant small T cells distributed throughout the interfollicular and paracortical areas, while several small follicles are largely CD3 negative, delineating their regressed architecture. The T-cell compartment appears reactive in distribution without atypical clusters. Taken together with the B-cell and plasma cell stains, the pattern supports preserved compartmentalization in Castleman disease-like changes seen in TAFRO syndrome. Evaluation for aberrant antigen loss (CD5, CD7) or a T follicular helper phenotype would be needed to exclude a T-cell lymphoma.

ddx.vs: AITL shows an expanded paracortex with atypical clear CD3-positive T cells that coexpress PD-1/CXCL13/CD10, extrafollicular CD21 FDC meshworks and clonal TCR, features not shown here.
PTCL shows diffuse effacement by atypical T cells often with loss of pan-T antigens such as CD5 or CD7, rather than a normal paracortical distribution around preserved follicles.

ddx.dx: Reactive paracortical hyperplasia (e.g., viral or dermatopathic)
ddx.vs: Paracortical hyperplasia has expanded T zones with immunoblasts or Langerhans cells but lacks the regressed follicles and hypervascularity of Castleman-type histology.
